author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Out of nowhere, Netflix and Until Dawn developer Supermassive Games announced a new The Conjuring game, and it's out next week.

The Conjuring: Unspoken releases on October 13 through Netflix, so you don't need any dedicated hardware or controller to play it.

The game is an "interactive paranormal investigation" experience where players decide how the story progresses based on the dialogue options they choose. Players use their phone to walk through the fictional Red Lion Inn to search for clues about "things that go bump in the night," Netflix said.

You play as demonologist Francesca Noakes, and you'll use an electromagnetic field reader, an infrared camera, and spirit box to hunt for ghosts.
title: A Scary-Looking New Conjuring Game Just Got Announced, And It’s Out Next Week On Netflix

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
During a town hall meeting today, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma spoke to staff to help reassure them following mass layoffs and studio closures related to the "reset" of the business.

Windows Central reports that Sharma told staff that Xbox is "making the right decisions" and that "after an all time low, we've started to return to growth," though she did not share any specifics. She added that Gears of War: E-Day, Minecraft Dungeons 2, and World of Warcraft: Forever had "strong" starts, though she did not share any specifics.

Sharm
title: Xbox Was At An “All Time Low,” But Is Now Growing Again CEO Says Without Providing Any Real Evidence

author: Tamoor Hussain
description:
The world is a complicated place, but, regardless of political leanings, I think we can all agree that in 2016 I was much younger than I am in 2026. The younger me was a much more patient person, especially when it came to playing video games. I relished the opportunity to go on whatever ride designers and developers had spent years meticulously crafting. These days, however, I find myself frantically looking for the shortest and quickest path to satisfaction. Time is a commodity and I am not rich in it. 

Maybe it's my patience wearing thin, or maybe it's the children who are wrong, but I find that games these days are working overtime to put as much distance between the player and the thing that makes playing it satisfying and worthwhile. Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is undoubtedly the best recent example of this happening. I love tactics games. I'm not great at them, but nevertheless, I relish the opportunity to
title: There’s Never Been A Better Time To Play Fire Emblem: Awakening

author: Jordan Ramée
description:
I've been loving Star Wars: Galactic Racer--I still cannot believe that a silly racing roguelite is one of my favorite games this year. But as it happens, I could have been enjoying it way more this entire time, because for the first 16 hours or so I've played, I've been playing all wrong: in third-person perspective.

I'm still not sure how I didn't know that Galactic Racer allows you to race from the perspective of your pilot, Shade. Like, obviously, it would. It's not an uncommon practice for an arcade racer to have the option to change your perspective from third- to first-person, so why wouldn't Galactic Racer also have that choice? But it wasn't until after I had finished my review and was excitedly talking about
title: You’re Likely Playing Star Wars: Galactic Racer All Wrong, Like I Did For My First 16 Hours

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Razer has officially revealed the next entry in its line of high-end gaming controllers, the Wolverine V4 for Xbox and PC. Geared toward competitive gamers--not that there's anything stopping you from using it to play Vampire Survivors--and it focuses primarily on polling performance and thumbstick sensor architecture.

One of the biggest changes is Razer choosing capacitive contactless sensors backed by a 16-bit analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for the thumbsticks, rather than the usual Hall Effect magnetic sensor. While Hall Effect thumbsticks are popular for their durability and for essentially eliminating stick drift, they can be prone to magnetic interference. Not a dealbreaker if you're playing at home, but in a competitive scene where victory is measured in fractions of a second, this can be an issue. In comparison, Razer is aiming to offer the same drift resistance, finer granularity, and smoother signal tracki
title: Razer’s Wolverine V4 Controller Is Overkill For Most Gamers, And That’s The Point

author: Ben Janca
description: Get a first look at high-speed combat on the planet Mars! Gear up, customize your ultimate mobile suit, and prepare to take on the Apocalypse in GUNDAM ROGUE ORBIT.
title: GUNDAM ROGUE ORBIT – Gameplay Walkthrough Trailer

author: Jordan Ramée
description:
Anakin Skywalker's purpose in the more recent Star Wars video games has continuously been hilarious to me.

For years, Anakin, who eventually became series antagonist Darth Vader, was characterized as something of a superhero who fell to darkness and became a supervillain. He was stronger than the typical guy, but we didn't see many examples of how that strength might be perceived outside of the scope of above-average combat prowess and reflexes. When it was released in 2016, Rogue One was a big departure to that, with its infamous ending scene that gives us a sense of what facing Darth Vader looks like to the average soldier. Turns out, it's terrifying. Anakin is basically an unstoppable demon, and the games since Rogue One have continued to refer back to this notion of him being a living legend. 

Whether it's adult Anakin fighting like a demigod, Vader rampaging like an unkillable
title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Continues The Hilarious Running Gag That Anakin Is The Boogeyman

author: Mark Delaney
description:
Soaring spaceships are no stranger to Star Wars video games, with thrilling dogfights at the core of both EA’s Battlefront and Star Wars: Squadrons. Yet very few George Lucas gaming adaptations have swapped aerial showdowns for laps around the intergalactic racetrack--until Galactic Racer.

Helmed by talent that worked on the vehicular sections of Battlefront and racing classics like Burnout and Need for Speed,  Galactic Racer is a game purely about the thrill of zooming past the Galaxy’s greatest racers, and thanks to its roguelike structure, this tournament plays dirty.

As you soar across the dunes of Jaaku and cruise across Lantaana’s lava-filled caverns, it’s important to race prepared. Where some racers may have the backing of insidious forces, we at GameSp
title: 7 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Played Star Wars: Galactic Racer

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Veteran video game actor Nolan North has addressed his future in the Call of Duty series, saying he hopes to reprise his character Dr. Edward Richtofen from Black Ops' popular Zombies mode.

If this does happen, it probably won't be soon. That's because, North said he believes 2027's Call of Duty game might be developed by Sledgehammer. Given that, a new Black Ops game might not come until 2028 at the soonest, but this is just conjecture.

Speaking at Gamergy in Puerto Rico (
title: Call Of Duty’s Richtofen Actor Wants Him To Come Back, Says 2027’s CoD Could Be From Sledgehammer

author: Ashley Bardhan
description:
Being a haunted doll must be difficult. You're missing an eyeball, and your lipstick makes you look more like a cannibal than a cherub. People make faces of disgust at you in the antique mall, and you want to tell them you're actually the unblemished soul of a 19th century nun named Eunice, but they speed away before you can. But if you were a haunted doll, you'd at least have solo developer Steelkrill Studio on your side, as its upcoming survival horror game Where Dolls Hang features real-life creepy dolls looking proudly injured. 

The dolls of Mexico's Isla de las Muñecas, the Island of the Dolls, have been through a lot over the past 80 years. Folklore suggests the bald dolls cobwebbed and nailed to the island's trees contain the spirit of a drowned little girl, who caretaker Don Julian Santana may or may not have made up. In any case, he spent much of his life fishing plastic Barbies and babies out of
title: Solo Horror Dev Makes A Creepy Connection To A Real Haunted Island In Mexico

author: Evan Campbell
description:
Sticker shock might be underselling it with GameStop's new used pricing for Sony's most powerful system. Starting today, the video game store is listing pre-owned PS5 Pros for $1,400, though GameStop Pro members only need to dish out $1,330. Basically, it's a $500 surcharge over a brand-new PS5 Pro and capitalizing on the fact that those are stock-constrained currently.

A generous take on GameStop's new strategy for used PS5 Pros is that the company's conditioning us ahead of the possibility that the PS6 could cost $1,000 or more.
title: GameStop Is Preparing Us For Next-Gen Pricing With $1,400 Used PS5 Pros

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
The next Survivors-like game--or Survivaton, as Vampire Survivors developer Poncle refers to them--is out soon, and it's threatening to cut into GTA 6 playtime. Warhammer Survivors launches November 10 on PC, consoles, and mobile devices, and you can also grab a new demo on PC via Steam right now.

Set in the grim (and dark) 41st millennium of the Warhammer 40,000 franchise, Warhammer Survivors sticks to the Vampire Survivors playbook: You'll fight all manner of Tyranid enemies that threaten the Imperium of Man, evolve your weapons, and die a lot before you're strong enough to start easily tanking the waves of heretical creatures. Extremis bosses will push your builds to the limit, and when it launches, the game will feature over 40 playable characters and an arsenal
title: Warhammer Survivors Is Launching Mere Days Before GTA 6, And I Respect The Audacity

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
If you're looking for GTA 6's $100 Ultimate Edition but don't want to pay that much, there is a way to get it for $80--if you meet a few requirements.

Costco has rolled out a nice new deal where you can get four $25 PlayStation Store gift cards for $80. Or you can
title: How To Get GTA 6’s $100 Edition For $80 Right Now

author: Steve Watts
description:
Final Fantasy Resonance is the first Final Fantasy game to use Square Enix's housemade "2D-HD" graphical style, as it revives the now-defunct mobile game Final Fantasy Brave Exvius and turns it into a full-fledged console RPG with all the trappings you'd expect. The demo was suitably impressive at showing how Resonance will tell an original Final Fantasy story that also pays homage to the entire series up to this point. But the element that sold me most was the sense of humor it seems to have about itself, which is encapsulated in one dialogue exchange.

Resonance leans heavily on nostalgia. This is most apparent in the use of Visions, which are heroes of past Final Fantasy games that can be equipped similarly to Final Fantasy 6's Espers. They level up while equipped, granting the user benefits and teaching new skills. To earn a Vision, you typically have to answer some questions related to a brief rundown of their stor
title: This One Hilarious Line Sold Me On Final Fantasy Resonance

author: Aaron Down
description:
The Coalition has gone all-out in Gears of War: E-Day when it comes to hiding various objects across the shooter's five acts. With 130 collectibles to gather -- the most of any Gears instalment to date -- there's a lot to keep an eye out for.

title: All Gears of War: E-Day Collectibles

author: Steve Watts
description:
Star Wars: Galactic Racer is getting well-deserved plaudits for its tense high-speed arcade racing action and an inventive roguelite structure that fits the genre like Vader's black glove. I have yet to complete the single-player campaign, but before I even realized it was a roguelite, the Star Wars racing game earned my respect with a statement of intent. Namely: It let me fail almost immediately.

As you may know if you've been following coverage including Jordan Ramée's excellent review, the campaign is not simply a linear sequence of races tied together with a story. Instead, it uses roguelike hooks, which means you earn permanent upgrades across runs, but mostly build your strategy as you go with the options given to you at any given time. At any point, you can crash out--sometimes l
title: Galactic Racer Immediately Taught Me A Hard Lesson, And I Have To Respect It

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Paramount has officially completed its $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, but the company's announcement of the deal closing did not contain a single mention of video games. That's notable because Warner Bros. Discovery is heavily invested in video games, and many may wonder what's coming next.

CEO David Ellison says he is a big gamer himself, but whether or not that means anything for the future of games at the new company, now known as Skydance, is unknown. Ellison, the son of billionaire Oracle founder Larry Ellison, courted controversy due to his family's dealings with Donald Trump and the current administration,
title: Warner Bros. Games Now Belongs To Skydance, But Company Makes No Mention Of That In Big Announcement

author: Ben Janca
description:
Experience the high-speed, high-stakes reinvention of racing set in a galaxy far, far away. Pilot a range of speeders and podracers as you make your way through the Galactic League, an unsanctioned racing circuit born in the lawless Outer Rim of the Star Wars galaxy. Developed by Fuse Games and published by Secret Mode, in collaboration with Lucasfilm Games.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer is now available worldwide on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC.
title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer – Official Launch Trailer

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Time flies by fast, especially if you're Sega's blue mascot, as 2026 marks the 35th anniversary of Sonic the Hedgehog. While Sega has various plans to commemorate the milestone, one of the most elegant is a hand-painted porcelain sculpture that is both graceful and expensive. Even if you can afford to shell out big bucks for this Blue Blur pottery, you'll still need luck on your side, as only 50 of these pieces are being made.

Sculpted by the artisans of the Japanese studio YOYOYO, this ornate piece costs a whopping $7,000. It comes with a certificate of authenticity, a wooden stand, and a wooden box, but you'll need to enter a lottery to have a chance to buy it.

So what makes this piece so special? To realize the idea of Sonic
title: Sega Announces $7,000 Sonic The Hedgehog Pottery, And I Can’t Stop Watching How It’s Made

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
The virtual reality market has grown over the years, and depending on your budget, there's probably a VR headset out there for you. But can your VR gaming budget stretch to over $1,000 for the entry-level Steam Frame headset, and is it even worthwhile? That's the question GameSpot's senior video producer Kurt Indovina set out to answer, and after spending some time with it, his main takeaway was that it's the best VR headset he's ever used, and possibly the last one he'll ever own.

"Having used this solid piece of tech for a couple of weeks now, it's been great to replay things like
title: Steam Frame Gets VR Right Where So Many Others Went Wrong

author: Steve Watts
description:
It's hard to overstate the impact of Wii Sports on Nintendo's fortunes. A simple motion-controlled game concept became a cultural phenomenon and arguably pulled the company back from the brink of a flagging game business. Switch Sports Resort is now the fifth game in the franchise, and while it still finds some depth in surprising places, the novelty is also wearing thin.

I got an extended hands-on with Switch Sports Resort, trying out a total of eight sports and activities from the selection, and giving me a good sampling of how this next sports game includes both competitive sporting events and free-roaming exploration around Wuhu Island. About half of the events were returning from previous Sports titles, and the others were new for this incarnation. So while there was a good sampling of new activities, my brief time with them prevented me from answering my biggest question: How much mileage will they all have colle
title: Switch Sports Resort Is An Overly Familiar Vacation

author: Callum Self
description:
Dragon’s Dogma 2 isn’t perfect, but I’d be lying if I said it wasn’t one of my favorite games of 2024. Climbing a giant monster and taking it down like you’re a supernaturally powered David against a monstrous Goliath is just fun, solidified into a game mechanic, and the combat only heightens the experience. With the Dark Arisen expansion giving me another reason to return to Battahl and, well, another reason to ignore the Pawn trailing behind me as I walk over the trail of corpses I’ve left in my wake, I’m ready to become the Arisen once again.

I won’t bore you with the base game's details—if you’re here, you’ve probably already played one of the best RPGs of recent years. Dark Arisen isn’t just a simple narrative patched onto the existing game, either. It’s the culmination of months of per
title: This Dragon’s Dogma 2: Dark Arisen Pre-Order Discount Gives You Another Reason To Ignore Your Pawn

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Star Wars: Galactic Racer is finally out, and so far, it might just be one of the best Star Wars games ever made. The new racing game has an attractive MSRP of $60, but if you're looking to grab it for the low price of nothing, you can play it for free through Amazon Luna starting today.

Amazon has announced that Prime members can stream the single-player campaign for free through Amazon Luna. "We've always believed Luna players deserve to be in the action from day one, and Star Wars: Galactic Racer makes that a reality for the first time,” Jeff Gattis, Head of Gaming at Amazon, said in a blog post. "Luna players can jump into the single-player campaign today without needing to own a console or wait for a lengthy download. It's exactly the kind of experience we want to deliver on Luna, and we think pl
title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Is Free To Play Now, If You Know Where To Look
